title: classify simple derivative zeros
stem: A differentiable function f has f'(x)=1(x-(-2))(x-(1)) for all real x, with -2<1. Which classification of its local extrema follows from the first derivative test?

choices.label: A
choices.text: f has a local minimum at x=-2 and a local maximum at x=1.
choices.rationale: This reverses the derivative sign changes: positive-to-negative makes a maximum and negative-to-positive a minimum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: f has a local maximum at x=-2 and a local minimum at x=1.
choices.rationale: Correct: For x<-2, between -2 and 1, and x>1, the derivative signs are positive, negative, positive. Thus x=-2 is a positive-to-negative switch and x=1 a negative-to-positive switch.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Both x=-2 and x=1 are local maxima because f' is zero at both.
choices.rationale: Zeros are candidates; the sign changes around each root determine opposite extremum types.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither zero of f' can be a local extremum because f is differentiable there.
choices.rationale: Differentiability does not prevent local extrema; these derivative sign reversals establish them.

title: interpret a derivative sign chart
stem: A graph of a continuous derivative f' crosses or touches the x-axis only at x=-2, 0, and 3. On the four successive intervals its signs are +,-,-,+. Which conclusion about f follows?

choices.label: A
choices.text: f has a local minimum at x=-2, a local maximum at x=3, and neither at x=0.
choices.rationale: The sign-switch directions are reversed: positive-to-negative is a local maximum, not a minimum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: f has a local maximum at x=-2, a local minimum at x=3, and neither type of extremum at x=0.
choices.rationale: Correct: Read derivative signs in x order: +,-,-,+. A + to - switch marks a maximum, - to + marks a minimum, and no sign switch at x=0 marks neither.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All three zeros are local extrema because f' is zero at each.
choices.rationale: A derivative zero without a sign reversal need not be a local extremum; inspect all adjacent intervals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No local extrema can be inferred because the numerical values of f at the zeros are unknown.
choices.rationale: The first derivative test uses signs of f', so explicit function values are unnecessary to classify local extrema.

title: classify even and odd derivative zeros
stem: A differentiable function g satisfies g'(x)=1(x-(1))²(x-(-2)) for all real x. Which statement about the stationary points x=1 and x=-2 is correct?

choices.label: A
choices.text: x=1 is a local minimum; x=-2 is not an extremum because the factor at -2 has odd multiplicity.
choices.rationale: The squared factor gives no derivative sign reversal at its root, while the simple factor does reverse sign at the other root.

choices.label: B
choices.text: x=-2 is a local maximum, and x=1 is also a local extremum because both factors vanish.
choices.rationale: The simple factor changes sign, but its extremum type is reversed here; the repeated root stays stationary without an extremum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: x=-2 is a local minimum; x=1 is stationary but not a local extremum because g' keeps its sign there.
choices.rationale: Correct: The squared factor at x=1 does not flip sign. Away from that point the sign of g' is the sign of 1(x-(-2)), which changes negative to positive at x=-2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neither point can be a local extremum because the derivative is a polynomial and therefore continuous.
choices.rationale: A continuous polynomial derivative can change sign at a simple root and create a local extremum.
